category: Purview, DLP & data security for Copilot
title: Set retention for Copilot interactions
problem: Compliance requires a defined retention period for AI prompts and responses.
steps: Inventory first: Purview > Data lifecycle management > Retention policies. Note every policy that uses the Teams chats location and was created before the Copilot split; older ones may still cover Copilot interactions implicitly.

New retention policy > select the 'Microsoft Copilot experiences' location (Microsoft 365 Copilot, Security Copilot, Copilot in Fabric, Copilot Studio). Other AI app locations (Enterprise AI apps, Other AI apps) only hold content when a collection policy captures it.
Set retain/delete period and scope to match the Teams-based coverage you are replacing, so nothing changes for compliance when the legacy policy stops applying.
Document in your records management plan which policy now governs Copilot, and the date the legacy Teams policy stops covering it (mid- to end of January 2027 per MC1481313).
pitfalls: From mid-January 2027 (completing by end of January), legacy Teams retention policies are treated as Teams-only and stop retaining or deleting Copilot interactions (MC1481313). Create the Copilot policy before then.
Deletion runs via a timer job (typically 1–7 days) and is suspended by any hold on the mailbox: another retention policy for the same location, Litigation Hold, delay hold or eDiscovery hold.
Do not verify retention by looking at Copilot chat history: Microsoft says visible messages are not an accurate reflection of whether content is retained or permanently deleted. Use eDiscovery.
Copilot memory is outside Purview retention policies; handle it in your AI use policy, not here.
done_when: A retention policy for the 'Microsoft Copilot experiences' location exists with the period and scope compliance asked for.
No compliance requirement depends on a legacy Teams retention policy to cover Copilot interactions.
An eDiscovery search scoped to Copilot interactions for a pilot user returns the expected items.
The policy is listed in your records management plan.

sources.title: Learn about retention for Copilot & AI apps
MC1481313: Legacy Teams retention policies that cover Copilot will be treated as Teams-only (Message Center archive)

troubleshooting.symptom: Copilot messages are still visible to the user after the retention period.
troubleshooting.cause: Expected: expired items are copied to SubstrateHolds by a timer job (typically 1–7 days), kept at least 1 day, and the delete is then relayed to the app; caching can delay it further.
troubleshooting.fix: Check for holds on the mailbox (other retention policy for the same location, Litigation Hold, delay hold, eDiscovery hold), and verify with eDiscovery rather than the app.

troubleshooting.symptom: An eDiscovery search finds no Copilot interactions for a user in scope.
troubleshooting.cause: Copilot content is stored in a hidden folder of the user's Exchange Online mailbox; users without such a mailbox, or outside the policy scope, are not covered.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the user's mailbox and that the policy's scope includes them, then search again.

rollback: To undo, set the new policy to Off or narrow its scope; the legacy Teams policy keeps covering Teams chats regardless. Deleting a retain policy can release content for deletion, so prefer disabling and agree changes with compliance.
